text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 3.9% today as oil prices retreated on improving diplomatic prospects in the Middle East. Over the past two days, crude oil has edged lower as Saudi Arabia and Iran engaged in de-escalation talks, reducing the geopolitical risk premium that had pushed prices higher earlier in the week. When oil prices fall, refiners like Marathon face lower margins on their core business—they buy crude at whatever the market price is, but the value of the gasoline and diesel they produce tends to move with it.

The broader pattern fits a classic risk-off sentiment: the stock had spiked to $475 on October 20th during peak Middle East tensions (when Brent crude hit a six-month high above $116), but has given back most of those gains as the acute crisis appeared to ease. At current refinery utilization of 93.4%, the company has capacity to capitalize on higher spreads, but those spreads compress when geopolitical fears subside and oil prices normalize.
